governed_construct: The sequence of top-level static ES import declarations (ImportDeclaration nodes, including `import type`) in one source file. Each declaration is classified by its module specifier: external package (any specifier not starting with '.', '/' or '@/', including scoped packages like '@nestjs/common' and node builtins like 'node:fs'), models ('@/models/...'), shared ('@/shared/...'), modules ('@/modules/...'), relative ('./' or '../'). A file with at least one import declaration is an instance.
interpretation: The rule fixes a group order: external < @/models/ < @/shared/ < @/modules/ < relative. A file is SATISFIED when, reading its import declarations in source order, the group rank never decreases (groups may be skipped, and several imports may share a group in any internal order). It is VIOLATED when any import declaration has a lower group rank than some earlier import declaration in the same file. It is NOT_APPLICABLE when the file has no import declarations. Only real ImportDeclaration nodes count: text that looks like an import inside comments or string/template literals is ignored, dynamic import() calls and require() calls are not import declarations, and export-from re-exports are not governed. A declaration split over several lines is one declaration classified by its specifier. Scoped npm packages ('@scope/pkg') are external, not alias imports; only the literal '@/' prefix denotes the project alias. Specifiers under other '@/' aliases not named by the rule are unclassified and do not affect the verdict (none of the fixtures use them).
